author: Coral Murphy Marcos and agencies
description:
Father of toddler killed in Erie mass shooting says reported gunman never seemed distressed or out of the ordinary

The man who killed eight people, before turning the gun on himself, in a mass shooting in a home in Erie, Pennsylvania, on Friday was a grandfather who had not shown signs that he was capable of such violence, according to people who knew the shooter.

A man whose toddler was among those killed said on Sunday that the man never seemed distressed or out of the ordinary, the Associated Press reports.

Continue reading...
title: Pennsylvania shooter who killed eight was a grandfather, says slain child’s dad

author: Nick Visser
description:
A second boy, 16, was also charged in relation to the stabbing death of a 30-year-old man in Mt Druitt

A thirteen-year-old boy has been charged with murder after a man was stabbed to death in Sydney’s west on Friday.

Emergency services were called to the suburb of Mt Druitt on Friday evening amid reports a man had been assaulted.

Continue reading...
title: Boy, 13, charged with murder after man stabbed to death in Sydney’s west

author: Guardian staff
description:
Follow the day’s news live

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Good morning, Krishani Dhanji with you here on our politics blog to cover another busy sitting week.

Time is quickly running out for the government who have a few key pieces of legislation they want to pass with only three joint sitting weeks left in the year and one Senate-only sitting week.

But right now, voters will only get advice from the independent PBO on the costs of the Coalition and Labor’s policies. They should get that same advice about One Nation’s policies.

One Nation has made no secret of how much they admire American and Argentinian-style wage policies, healthcare policies and cuts to the public service.
title: Politics live: Greens call for US execution live stream to be blocked; Flydubai pilot’s Australia links ‘disturbing’

author: Press Association
description:
Move comes after criticism of remarks in support of football club’s owners following financial regulations breach ruling

Andy Burnham has said he will publish all details of his dealings with Manchester City in his previous mayoral role after his intervention in support of the football club’s owners raised eyebrows.

Kemi Badenoch, the Conservative party leader, had urged the prime minister to publish everything related to his work with the club as Greater Manchester mayor and the Liberal Democrats wrote to him asking him to release minutes of meetings and declare all hospitality gifts received from owners of Manchester City.

Continue reading...
title: Andy Burnham to publish all details of his dealings with Manchester City

author: Associated Press
description:
Senior official says president and US secretary of state are ‘extremely pissed off’ by conduct of US envoy to Greece

Donald Trump and Marco Rubio, the secretary of state, are considering firing US ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle after a series of reports alleging she has engaged in improper and possibly illegal conduct before and during her tenure in Athens.

A senior US official said Sunday that Trump and Rubio are “extremely pissed off” by Guilfoyle’s reported conduct and would likely decide on what action to take this week after Monday’s federal holiday.

Continue reading...
title: Trump and Rubio weigh firing Kimberly Guilfoyle after reports of improper conduct

author: Eric Berger
description:
Democratic Senate candidate’s remarks come as Trump has long baselessly claimed his 2020 election loss was stolen

Democrats must “win by massive numbers” during November’s federal midterm elections because Donald Trump and his Republican allies are bound to try to sow doubt about the integrity of the results, Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed of Michigan said on Sunday.

El-Sayed’s comments on NBC’s Meet the Press came with the Democrats favored to win control of the House of Representatives during the 3 November midterms – and polls show that the party could also win Senate seats in states that traditionally elect Republicans and gain a majority there, too.
title: Abdul El-Sayed: Democrats must ‘win by massive numbers’ to fend off Trump election denial

author: Luke Harding
description:
Ukrainian president earlier rejected US call for Kyiv to stop bombing oil refineries, saying Moscow must first end attacks on energy infrastructure

  • US politics – live updates

Donald Trump has announced an energy ceasefire between Ukraine and Russia, apparently without consulting Volodymyr Zelenskyy, who said the deal to stop long-range attacks was “news to me”.

In a social media post, the US president claimed the two sides had reached an agreement. “Effective immediately, there is an ENERGY CEASEFIRE in the War between Russia and Ukraine. Both parties have agreed. Do not break it!” he wrote on Truth Social.

Continue reading...
title: Trump announces partial ceasefire in Ukraine war as Zelenskyy says deal is ‘news to me’

author: Simon Goodley
description:
Analysts say fuel will take weeks to ship and is too small to affect prices, with the full deal unlikely to be met given damage to Russian refineries

  • Zelenskyy rejects Trump claim of Ukraine-Russia ‘energy ceasefire’

Donald Trump’s deal with Vladimir Putin to temporarily lift sanctions on US imports of Russian diesel will have little “meaningful” impact for motorists and businesses in the US and overseas, energy and foreign policy analysts have predicted.

The US president infuriated the Ukraine president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, as he took to his Truth Social network on Friday, saying the agreement with his Russia counterpart to supply millions of tonnes of diesel was essential to reduce fuel prices in the US, which have s
title: Trump’s deal with Putin will have little impact on US diesel prices, experts warn

author: Fran Lawther
description:
US president provides no details of alleged agreement in social media announcement that came just after Ukraine’s president spoke to US media

Donald Trump has claimed Russia and Ukraine have agreed to an ”energy ceasefire”, though the US president gave no details of the purported agreement.

Trump made the announcement on his Truth Social account shortly after Ukraine’s president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, told ABC on Sunday that Ukraine was ready for a ceasefire, including on energy infrastructure.

Continue reading...
title: Donald Trump claims Ukraine and Russia have agreed to ‘energy ceasefire’ – live updates

author: William Christou in Jerusalem
description:
Official says coalition will ‘respond firmly’ as Houthis warn people to avoid Saudi airports and US considers intervening

  • Middle East crisis live – latest updates

  • Analysis: attack will force rethink of Trump strategy

The Saudi-led coalition in Yemen has vowed to retaliate after a suspected Houthi missile attack on Riyadh airport killed 12 people and wounded more than 300, as Donald Trump said the US could join its military campaign.

Saudi Arabia blamed the Iran-allied Houthi rebel movement for the strike on the airport on Saturday, which damage
title: Saudi coalition vows retaliation after deadly Houthi attack on Riyadh airport

author: Amanda Meade Media correspondent
description:
Exclusive: As William ‘Rob’ Gilfillan was about to go on trial for sex offences against two schoolgirls, his barrister told a judge his client’s history was easily discoverable online

  • Sign up for Guardian Australia’s free weekly media newsletter here

The Australian’s podcast Shadow of Doubt led to a delay of 10 months for the sex offence trial of a “sadistic” paedophile already serving a 48-year jail term for abusing his daughter, court documents have revealed.

William “Rob” Gilfillan, a former physical education teacher, was to stand trial in Victoria in February last year on five counts of indecent assault and sexual penetration of a person u
title: The Australian’s Shadow of Doubt podcast delayed ‘sadistic’ paedophile’s trial, court documents reveal

author: Patrick Commins
description:
Australia does have a migration challenge – but it’s not what One Nation and the Coalition think it is

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

Australia is flirting with the idea of something it has never done: deliberately driving net overseas migration into reverse.

In the history of our immigrant nation, extended periods of more people leaving our shores than arriving have only happened during convulsive moments: economic collapses, wars, and pandemics.
title: Australia has never driven migration into reverse by design. Would slamming the brakes on be calamitous?

author: Tom McIlroy Political editor
description:
Minor party plans to drive a tough bargain in exchange for support for digital duty of care legislation

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

The Greens will push Labor to dramatically toughen new laws designed to rein in big tech, calling for individuals to have the right to take platforms to court and win financial compensation.

As Labor prepares to introduce its planned digital duty of care laws into parliament this week, the Greens say they will drive a tough bargain in exchange for support, including pushing for fines by the eSafety commissioner to be levied as a percentage of c
title: Greens gear up for fight with Labor as Sarah Hanson-Young pushes to strengthen laws to rein in big tech

author: Associated Press
description:
At least four deaths linked to storm amid warnings of flash flooding that could stretch into Appalachians

Nearly 396,000 customers across the Florida Panhandle and southern Alabama remained without power early Sunday as remnants of Hurricane Isaias moved north, where widespread moderate to heavy rainfall was expected across the central Appalachians and mid-Atlantic region.

Heavy rainfall associated with the storm could bring isolated flash flooding and strong wind gusts and remain a threat across the south-eastern US, especially near the southern Appalachians, according to the National Weather Service (NWS). That could bring scattered power outages and downed trees and power lines. Life-threatening surf and rip current conditions were expected to continue along the Gulf and south-eastern Atlantic coasts.
title: Thousands without power in Florida and Alabama as Isaias moves north

author: Associated Press
description:
Comments were among the most direct overtures by Trump to woo Democratic senator into his Republican party

Donald Trump on Saturday openly encouraged Democratic US senator John Fetterman to switch parties and become a Republican just weeks before the federal midterm elections could reshape control of Congress.

“I’d love to see him as a Republican,” the presidents told reporters at Joint Base Andrews as he returned to Washington DC from a rally in Tennessee. “He does better as a Republican than he does as a Democrat.”

Guardian staff contributed reporting

Continue reading...
title: Trump urges John Fetterman to switch parties: ‘I’d love to see him as a Republican’

author: Patrick Wintour
description:
US president’s plan to park the conflicts in Iran and Yemen, while blaming Ukraine for high diesel prices, has unravelled

  • Middle East crisis live - latest updates

The reckless missile attack on King Khalid international airport in Riyadh on Saturday did not just export the death and misery inside Yemen to Saudi Arabia, it also left Donald Trump forced to reconsider his diplomatic and political strategy designed to take him into the midterm elections next month.

The US president plan’s had only been unveiled on Saturday. It was to blame what he described as “a world problem” – spiralling diesel prices – on the Ukrainian president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, saying his attacks on Russian oil refineries were the cause. He was going to keep the political temperature down on his war of choice in Iran and its sp
title: Houthi attack on Riyadh airport will force rethink of Donald Trump’s strategy

author: Eve Livingston Scotland correspondent
description:
Part of site of First Hampden in Glasgow is up for rent and campaigners want to turn it into a community hub

Fans of Scotland’s national football team may not have had many reasons to celebrate in recent years, but that hasn’t always been the case. Almost 150 years ago, in 1878, the team moved into their first home in a Glasgow ground known as First Hampden and promptly won every game they played there.

As well as being celebrated as Scotland’s “tartan fortress”, First Hampden, about half a mile from where Hampden Park sits today in south Glasgow, is widely considered the world’s first purpose-built international football stadium. Many features now commonplace in grounds around the world – including season tickets, turnstiles and pavilions – have long been thought to have originated there.

Continue re
title: Campaign launched to safeguard site of first home of Scotland’s national football team

author: Diane Taylor
description:
As ‘one in, one out’ scheme ends, refugees still want to cross the Channel despite French police aggression and hostile welcomes

The smuggler works quickly. Using a small shovel, he digs up a dinghy buried in a sand dune on a beach not far from Boulogne-sur-Mer, assembles it and affixes a motor in record time.

“I never saw anyone work like this,” says Amad, from Iraq, one of a group of about 30 asylum seekers waiting to cross the Channel. “The UK government wants to stop the smugglers, but they are smart. They have plan A, plan B and plan C, so there is always a way for them to get people across this sea. For as long as asylum seekers will pay them, there is too much money involved for them to give up.”

Continue reading...
title: People smugglers are still profiting from small boats. Can the UK fix the crisis?

author: Hannah Al-Othman North of England correspondent
description:
Bev Craig pledges £2m in funding to nurture local artists by improving access to rehearsal and production space

The Manchester mayor, Bev Craig, has said the city’s music scene is about more than just Oasis, as she announced funding to nurture a diverse range of local artists, be they “guitar bands or not”.

Craig pledged the £2m investment funding in Greater Manchester, as the city region hosted a conference for the creative industries at MediaCity in Salford.

Continue reading...
title: There’s more to our music than Oasis, says Manchester mayor

author: Eric Berger
description:
As raw milk industry experiences record growth, experts say it might contain pathogens that can sicken people

As raw milk becomes increasingly popular among Americans, there have been several recent disease outbreaks tied to the product, alarming public health officials.

Last week, the American Academy of Pediatrics called for a ban on sales of unpasteurized milk in the United States.

Continue reading...
title: Physicians’ group calls for ban on raw milk – as it’s becoming increasingly popular in the US

author: Tobi Thomas Health and inequalities correspondent
description:
Trump’s ‘big, beautiful bill’ spending cuts will be fully felt next year, but hospitals are already feeling the squeeze

Maternity wards across the United States are facing a wave of closures as cuts to federal Medicaid funding take effect, experts have warned.

According to analysis by the non-profit Protect Our Care, 52 maternity wards have closed since the HR1 bill was announced in July 2025, with a further eight having announced their upcoming closure.

Continue reading...
title: US maternity wards face wave of closures as Medicaid cuts kick in

author: Associated Press
description:
Pontiff says it was detected at an early stage and procedure will take place in the first days of this week

Pope Leo XIV has said he will undergo surgery in the coming days to remove a nodular lesion on his lung that was recently discovered during medical checks.

The 71-year-old said the nodule was found at an early stage and was “circumscribed” or well localised. The Vatican later said Leo would undergo surgery in the first days of this week, with an expected recovery time of a week.

Continue reading...
title: Pope Leo to have surgery to remove nodule on his lung

author: Aletha Adu Political correspondent
description:
Defence secretary backs Ukrainian president and says priority is to maintain western unity over Russia conflict

Britain stands behind Volodymyr Zelenskyy, the defence secretary has said, after Donald Trump called for the Ukrainian president to be replaced and the US announced a controversial agreement to buy Russian diesel.

Wes Streeting said Ukrainians alone should be able to decide who leads their country as he indicated Trump was facing domestic political pressure over fuel prices before next month’s midterm elections.

Continue reading...
title: Britain stands behind Zelenskyy, says Streeting after Trump’s call for new leader in Ukraine

author: Frances Mao
description:
US president Donald Trump says he is weighing whether the US will join Saudi strikes against the Iran-backed Houthis

There’s been a strong condemnation of this morning of the Houthi’s deadly strike on Saudi Arabia’s largest airport. Global leaders say attacks on civilians must stop.

UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres said he was “deeply shocked” by Saturday’s strike.

Continue reading...
title: Middle East crisis live: Houthis warn passengers against using Saudi airport after deadly attack on Riyadh

author: Donna Ferguson
description:
Toxicology helplines report 42% increase in calls involving animals poisoned by drugs and nicotine

A record number of pets are ingesting recreational drugs and requiring veterinary care in the UK, figures shared with the Guardian reveal.

Last year, the UK’s only emergency poison centre for animals received its highest ever number of calls involving animals poisoned by cannabis, cocaine, magic mushrooms and nicotine, and it is on course to do so again this year.

Continue reading...
title: ‘She was swaying, zoning out’: UK pets poisoned in record numbers by illicit drugs

author: Ramon Antonio Vargas
description:
Republican Christopher Paul is running unopposed for seat despite allegations he raped two girls 20 years ago

A candidate for police chief in a small Louisiana town candidate is on course to be elected unopposed despite two charges of child rape pending against him, leaving his community to weigh whether to convert the position into an appointed office rather than one determined at the ballot box.

Christopher Paul, a Republican who on 6 August signed up to run for chief of police in the south-western Louisiana village of Elizabeth, was arrested on 8 September on allegations that he raped two girls in 2005 and 2006.

Continue reading...
title: Man accused of child rape set to become police chief in small Louisiana town

author: Robert Tait in Washington
description:
David McCloskey’s new book depicts a calamitous collapse of the ‘special relationship’ – could things get darker still?

The “special relationship”, the time-honored emotional bond between the US and Britain that has sustained through war and peace, is in trouble.

The ties of history, culture and language that have bridged an ocean and bound the two countries politically for generations are fraying as perhaps never before – strained relentlessly by Donald Trump, who has gleefully sacrificed traditional alliances and diplomatic niceties on the altar of his “America first” agenda.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Under tremendous strain’: CIA analyst turned spy novelist on a fraying US-UK alliance

author: Guardian staff
description:
Family and friends say Melbourne man should be remembered for ‘immense joy he brought to so many people’s lives’

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

An Australian trekker who was last seen on a remote South American hiking trail has been found dead, his family have said.

Jordan Yap, 30, last made contact with friends and family on 14 September ahead of a planned 10-day solo trek along Peru’s Huayhuash mountain range, 400km north-east of Lima.

Continue reading...
title: Missing Australian hiker Jordan Yap last seen on remote trail found dead in Peru

author: Josh Butler
description:
Preferences proved the sticking point at the conference as conservatives face the prospect of a third successive election defeat

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

Many mainstream Australians would feel as if they’d been dropped in a foreign country at the Conservative Political Action Conference, lost amid oblique references to transgender swimmers, blue hair, women’s bathrooms, jokes about falling off stages and Matt Canavan in hi-vis and speed dealer sunnies.

It’s an interesting spectacle. At this year’s conference i
title: A Trump impersonator and opera singers: CPAC was a spectacle, but the right still can’t agree how to take down Labor

author: Australian Associated Press
description:
Anthony Albanese speaks at Australian War Memorial event commemorating 25th anniversary of country’s involvement in the conflict

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Anthony Albanese has honoured Australian troops who served in Afghanistan, using the 25th anniversary of the country’s involvement in the conflict to describe their heroism as a fight for “who we are as a people”.

The prime minister joined hundreds of veterans, family members and dignitaries at a commemoration of the start of the campaign in Canberra on Sunday, with nation’s most decorated living soldier and accused war criminal Ben Roberts-Smith among the crowd at the Australian War Memorial.
title: Ben Roberts-Smith attends Canberra event honouring Australian troops who served in Afghanistan

author: Ben Smee
description:
Club issues brief statement about Lachie Cowan and Will Hayward, saying latter suffered minor cut to head after a fall

Carlton football club has said two of its players, Lachie Cowan and Will Hayward, required treatment in hospital on Sunday morning in “separate circumstances”.

The club released a statement on Sunday after reports in several media outlets that unnamed players had been taken to hospital by ambulance after a night out. Guardian Australia contacted Carlton seeking comment on the reports.

Continue reading...
title: Two Carlton players treated in hospital after needing care for ‘separate circumstances’

author: Uwa Ede-Osifo
description:
Deceased were all members of the same family, officials say, and one of victims placed the initial emergency call

Five people were shot and killed in an apparent murder-suicide at a residence in Georgia on Friday, authorities say.

The deceased were family members who lived at the home in Douglas, a city in south Georgia.

Continue reading...
title: Five people shot and killed in apparent murder-suicide, Georgia police say
